doc.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

chapter: Early life and path to music
title: What his parents and grandmother did for a living
summary: His mother supervised at Harlem Hospital, his grandmother catered there, and his father was a chef at Horn and Hardart.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What did your parents do for a living?

Mom was a supervisor at Harlem Hospital, which was like right down the street. Grandmom was a head caterer in the kitchen. And the one thing I can always remember about that is around Thanksgiving and Christmas we’d get this phone call and she’d be working and she’d say “come now” and we’d run over there and she’d have like — because they were going to throw it away anyway, all this surplus food — so she just dumped all of this stuff on us and I can always remember Thanksgiving and Christmas we had a lot of food because of her. And my dad, he separated and divorced like early on when we were young, my dad also worked, as a matter of fact also worked as a chef in a place called Horn and Hardart, I don’t know if you know that chain — it was a chain of cafeterias.
Horn and Hardart. And it’s like really, I don’t think they’re in business anymore. And he worked as a chef there. He was not musically inclined. He liked it but —
